newsitem.title: USA: L.A. wage plan could cost taxpayers $130 mln - study.
newsitem.headline: L.A. wage plan could cost taxpayers $130 mln - study.

text.p: A controversial Los Angeles wage control proposal would increase taxpayer costs by up to $130 million a year, forcing cuts to city services, according to a study released on Wednesday.
"This proposal will cost Los Angeles taxpayers as much as $130 million in tax increases and program cuts," said Spectrum Economics economist Richard Carlson, who authored the report.
The proposal, which is being considered by the city council, would require a minimum wage of $9.50 per hour for employees of businesses contracting with the city or subsidized by the city.
By increasing costs to contractors to perform the same services at a higher rate, businesses would have to change the composition of their workforce, Carlson said in the report.

Contractors would have to hire more skilled, better educated employees to perform jobs that otherwise would be filled by less skilled labor, the report said. As a result of these changes, 50 to 70 percent of the least educated workers would lose their jobs, the report concluded.

"This proposal would force small, minority and women-owned businesses to downsize their workforces to make up for the increase in the cost of doing business in Los Angeles," Carlson said. "The proposal spells bad news for small businesses and low-income, unskilled workers."
